completionSummary: Wyoming coverage now includes 23 routes spanning four major basins plus Yellowstone/Lewis-Shoshone. Five Seedskadee Green River access-to-access sections are eligible for conservative minimum-only scoring because USFWS ties the 700 cfs lower context and 800 cfs summer minimum to direct gauge 09211200. The remaining 18 routes stay planning-only; Alpine Canyon retains mixed-source flow cues without a hard safety floor.

baseline.overlapFinding: The 15 river cards remain distinct adjacent access-to-access sections; the overlap audit found three near-collinear adjacent pairs and five shared endpoints, with no duplicate endpoint pair. Eight lake/reservoir/wilderness cards are separate same-launch or lake-corridor itineraries with different waterbodies, access controls, and trip value; none duplicates an existing Wyoming river reach. Boysen, Jenny, Lewis-Shoshone, and Glendo close distinct basin, park, and trip-type gaps.

strategy.publicationPosture: Use scored minimum-only eligibility only for the five Seedskadee sections whose USFWS operating guidance is tied to direct gauge 09211200. A direct gauge alone does not justify scoring; all other Wyoming routes remain planning-only until route-specific thresholds are defensible.
strategy.thresholdPosture: Use minimum-only models and omit numeric cutoffs unless a manager or recognized paddling source ties a practical floor or clearly labeled planning cue to the selected gauge. Alpine Canyon uses a corroborated 1,800 cfs runnable-floor cue and 6,500 cfs preferred lower cue; neither is a safety guarantee. Never infer a ceiling from ordinary historical flow.
strategy.accessPosture: Publish only named NPS, USFS, USFWS, BLM, WGFD, state-park, or municipal launches. Preserve an official parking or campground anchor when it intentionally represents a carry/staging point and label the offset.
strategy.imagePosture: Prefer NPS, USFWS, USGS, USFS, or clearly licensed Wikimedia route imagery. Same-river or regional context must be labeled as context and must not imply the exact reach.
strategy.geometryPosture: Generate one canonical route asset per published card, inspect endpoint connection and water-corridor shape, and withhold any route whose access or geometry cannot be defended.

initialWithholdingRules: Do not publish Yellowstone River reaches inside Yellowstone National Park because park boating restrictions and closures require a separate rule review.
Do not publish Wind River Canyon or tribal-reservation-dependent reaches without explicit current permission and public access evidence.
Do not publish a bridge shoulder, fishing easement, or informal bank as a launch merely because it is near water.
Do not combine adjacent Grand Teton or Seedskadee sections into one card when their difficulty, float time, or safe operational boundary differs.
Withhold Southgate-to-Flagg Snake whitewater until a current public Southgate launch control and route-specific geometry are confirmed; NPS describes it as an advanced Class III run.
Publish lake and reservoir routes only as planning-only trips with explicit wind/cold-water/carry controls, same-launch or shoreline turnaround boundaries, and route-scoped curated geometry.

Publish the Lewis-Shoshone channel only as an expert planning route: the upstream shallow mile may require wading/lining, no road take-out exists at Shoshone, and overnight travel requires a Yellowstone backcountry permit.
